title: Where the Weight Presses: The Centre of Pressure, the Zero Moment Point of an Accelerating Body, and the Acceleration the Feet Can Allow

artifact.note: where a body presses on the ground: the centre of pressure from the forces on the feet (the mean of their places weighted by force); the zero moment point of a body of height h whose centre is accelerating horizontally at a (the centre of mass moved back by h over g times a, for a body that does not turn), which is where the centre of pressure must be for the body to be in balance; the margin of that point inside the feet that are down (a polygon for three or four feet, a line for two); and the greatest acceleration in a direction that keeps the point inside, with its agreement with the tipping limit of 33-05
